'''Sectigo''' is an American [[Computer security|cybersecurity]] company specializing in digital certificates and automated certificate lifecycle management.<ref name="Gifford">{{cite journal |last1=Gifford |first1=Jeff |title=Scottsdale cybersecurity firm doubles footprint with acquisition; plus more M&A deals |journal=Phoenix Business Journal |date=February 3, 2025 |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/phoenix/news/2025/02/03/sectigo-acquires-entrust-certificate-business.html}}</ref> It is one of the ten largest [[certificate authority|certificate authorities]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Omolola |first=Olamide |title=Measurement and Analysis of Automated Certificate Reissuance |date=2021 |volume=12671 |pages=161–174 |editor-last=Hohlfeld |editor-first=Oliver |url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-030-72582-2_10 |access-date=2026-07-30 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |language=en |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-72582-2_10 |isbn=978-3-030-72581-5 |last2=Roberts |first2=Richard |last3=Ashiq |first3=Md. Ishtiaq |last4=Chung |first4=Taejoong |last5=Levin |first5=Dave |last6=Mislove |first6=Alan |editor2-last=Lutu |editor2-first=Andra |editor3-last=Levin |editor3-first=Dave|journal=Passive and Active Measurement|url-access=subscription }}</ref> It provides public [[Root certificate|root certificates]] distributed with operating systems,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-06-12 |title=Sectigo Root Certificate Expiration Issue |url=https://blog.dnsimple.com/2020/06/sectigo-expired-root-certificate/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=DNSimple}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sectigo Public Root CAs migration |url=https://www.sectigo.com/sectigo-public-root-cas-migration |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Sectigo |language=en}}</ref> and it issues [[Public key certificate|public key certificates]] for websites. Formerly known as '''Comodo Certification Authority''' ('''Comodo CA'''), the company was founded under [[Comodo Group]] and was later acquired by [[Francisco Partners]] in 2017 and by [[GI Partners]] in 2020. Comodo CA was rebranded to Sectigo in 2018. The company has been headquartered in [[Scottsdale, Arizona]] since 2023.

==History and operations==

===Comodo CA===
Sectigo was established as Comodo Certification Authority (Comodo CA), a [[certificate authority]] (CA) business under the parent company [[Comodo Group]], which was founded by [[Melih Abdulhayoğlu]] in 1998.<ref name="Duckett">{{cite news |last1=Duckett |first1=Chris |title=Comodo CA sold to private equity as DigiCert completes Symantec CA purchase |url=https://www.zdnet.com/article/comodo-ca-sold-to-private-equity-as-digicert-completes-symantec-ca-purchase/ |work=[[ZDNET]] |date=October 31, 2017}}</ref><ref name="Kerner">{{cite news |last1=Kerner |first1=Sean Michael |title=Francisco Partners Acquires Comodo's Certificate Authority Business |url=https://www.eweek.com/security/francisco-partners-acquires-comodo-s-certificate-authority-business/ |work=[[eWeek]] |date=October 31, 2017}}</ref> Comodo Group and Comodo CA contributed to the [[Internet Engineering Task Force]] standard for [[DNS Certification Authority Authorization]] Resource Records.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6844|title=DNS Certification Authority Authorization – Comodo|year=2013|doi=10.17487/RFC6844|access-date=14 January 2013|last1=Hallam-Baker|first1=P.|last2=Stradling|first2=R.|s2cid=46132708|doi-access=free}}</ref>

In March 2011, a user account with an affiliate registration authority was compromised and was used to create a new user account that issued nine [[Certificate signing request|certificate signing requests]].<ref name="comodo inc1">{{cite web|url=https://www.comodo.com/Comodo-Fraud-Incident-2011-03-23.html|title=Report of incident on 15-MAR-2011: Update 31-MAR-2011|publisher=Comodo group|access-date=24 March 2011}}</ref> See {{Section link|Xcitium|Certificate hacking}}.

In 2016, Comodo CA launched the [[Cloud computing|cloud]]-based Comodo Certificate Manager, a [[digital certificate]] management platform to help companies manage [[Internet of things]] (IoT) devices.<ref name="FP" /><ref name="ODonnell">{{cite news |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Lindsey |title=Francisco Partners Acquires IoT Security Company Comodo's SSL Business, Bill Holtz Appointed CEO |url=https://www.crn.com/news/internet-of-things/300094746/francisco-partners-acquires-iot-security-company-comodos-ssl-business-bill-holtz-appointed-ceo |work=[[CRN (magazine)|CRN]] |date=October 31, 2017}}</ref>

Comodo CA was acquired by [[Francisco Partners]] in 2017. Comodo CA and Comodo Group were legally and operationally separated. Abdulhayoğlu kept a minority ownership stake, took an observer role on Comodo CA's [[board of directors]], and continued to operate Comodo Group as a distinct security business.<ref name=Duckett/><ref name=Kerner/> (Comodo Group rebranded as [[Xcitium]] in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fernando|first=Chris|date=2022-07-07|title=Comodo Security Solutions Rebrands to Xcitium|url=https://securityreviewmag.com/?p=24490|access-date=2025-06-10|language=en-US|website=Security Review}}</ref>) As part of the 2017 purchase, Bill Holtz became the CEO, and [[Bill Conner]] of the cybersecurity company [[SonicWall]] was named the [[Chair (officer)|chair]].<ref name=Duckett/><ref name="FP">{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Ian |title=Francisco Partners acquires Comodo CA business |url=https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/2017/11/01/francisco-partners-acquires-comodo-ca-business/ |date=November 1, 2017 |work=Enterprise Times}}</ref>

The Comodo CA business initially continued with the Comodo brand, as leadership considered a rebrand.<ref name=Kerner/> Comodo CA issued approximately 55 million certificates in 2017,<ref name=Duckett/> bringing the total number of certificates issued to approximately 91 million, distributed to approximately 200,000 customers in 150 countries.<ref name="Kovacs">{{cite news |last1=Kovacs |first1=Eduard |title=Comodo Sells Certificate Business to Private Equity Firm |url=https://www.securityweek.com/francisco-partners-acquires-comodo-ca/ |work=Security Week |date=October 31, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Francisco Partners Takes Majority Stake in Comodo's Certificate Authority Business |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/francisco-partners-takes-majority-stake-in-comodos-certificate-authority-business-1509466885 |work=The Wall Street Journal |date=October 31, 2017}}</ref> In 2018, the company acquired Atlanta-based CodeGuard to help customers protect websites from [[malware]] via [[backup]], [[IT disaster recovery]], and [[Computer maintenance|maintenance]].<ref name=Murphy/><ref name="Novinson">{{cite news |last1=Novinson |first1=Michael |title=Comodo CA Buys Website Disaster Recovery Startup CodeGuard |url=https://www.crn.com/news/security/comodo-ca-buys-website-disaster-recovery-startup-codeguard |work=CRN |date=August 16, 2018}}</ref>

===Sectigo===
Comodo CA rebranded as Sectigo in 2018, in part to avoid confusion with the parts of Comodo Group not acquired by Francisco Partners.<ref name="Murphy">{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Ian |title=Comodo CA becomes Sectigo and expands to cover IoT |url=https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/2018/11/02/comodo-ca-becomes-sectigo-and-expands-to-cover-iot/ |work=Enterprise Times |date=November 2, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=November 1, 2018 |title=Comodo CA changes its name to Sectigo |url=https://www.thesslstore.com/blog/comodo-ca-changes-its-name-to-sectigo/ |access-date=May 12, 2025 |work=The SSL Store}}</ref> The company also began supporting IoT devices and introduced new products in 2018.<ref name=Murphy/> In 2019, Sectigo announced changes to its [[channel partner]] program and launched additional certifications, products, rewards, and tools.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Todd |first=Daniel |date=January 10, 2019 |title=Sectigo revamps its channel partner programme |url=https://www.itpro.com/channel/365272/sectigo-revamps-its-channel-partner-programme |access-date= |website=ITPro |language=en}}</ref> The company also acquired the [[West Des Moines, Iowa]]-based IoT security provider Icon Labs,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Novinson |first1=Michael |title=Sectigo Buys Embedded OEM And IoT Security Vendor Icon Labs |url=https://www.crn.com/news/security/sectigo-buys-embedded-oem-and-iot-security-vendor-icon-labs |work=CRN |date=May 9, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Sectigo Acquires Icon Labs |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/48597875 |work=Computer Security Update |date=June 2019 |volume=20 |number=6 |pages=2–5 |jstor=48597875 |via=[[JSTOR]]}}</ref> which merged with Sectigo's IoT Security Platform and continued as a brand and subsidiary under Sectigo.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Corfield |first1=Gareth |title=Cert authority Sectigo whisks infosec biz Icon Labs into IoT security kit |url=https://www.theregister.com/2019/05/09/sectigo_buys_icon_labs/ |work=[[The Register]] |date=May 9, 2019}}</ref><ref name=Arghire>{{cite news |last1=Arghire |first1=Ionut |title=Sectigo Acquires IoT Security Firm Icon Labs |url=https://www.securityweek.com/sectigo-acquires-iot-security-firm-icon-labs/ |work=Security Week |date=May 13, 2019}}</ref>

[[GI Partners]] acquired Sectigo in 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |author=Dan Kobialka |date=September 18, 2020 |title=Identity Management Acquisition: GI Partners Buys Sectigo |url=https://www.msspalert.com/cybersecurity-news/gi-partners-acquires-sectigo/ |access-date=May 12, 2025 |work=MSSP Alert}}</ref> Sectigo had approximately 700,000 customers at the time.<ref name="Vinn">{{cite news |last1=Vinn |first1=Milana |title=GI's purchase of Sectigo values the company at ~$900m |url=https://www.pehub.com/gis-purchase-of-sectigo-values-the-company-at-900m/ |work=PE Hub |date=September 18, 2020}}</ref> In late 2020, Sectigo announced the purchase of the SSL certificate and web security provider SSL247, which operated in Europe and Latin America, as well as the Netherlands-based SSL certificates and digital signatures provider Xolphin. Both of the businesses initially continued to operate as brands under Sectigo.<ref name="Coker">{{cite journal |last1=Coker |first1=James |title=Sectigo Acquires SSL247 and Xolphin |journal=Infosecurity Magazine |date=December 3, 2020 |url=https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/sectigo-acquires-ssl247-and-xolphin/}}</ref>

Sectigo acquired [[Scottsdale, Arizona|Scottsdale]]-based SiteLock in 2021.<ref name=Gifford/> SiteLock had approximately 70 employees in the [[Phoenix metropolitan area]]. The acquisition of SiteLock increased Sectigo's employee count to 450 globally.<ref name="Blye">{{cite journal |last1=Blye |first1=Andy |title=Cybersecurity firm SiteLock to be acquired by New Jersey buyer as lawsuit against GoDaddy continues |journal=[[Phoenix Business Journal]] |date=May 4, 2021 |url=https://www.bizjournals.com/phoenix/news/2021/05/04/cybersecurity-provide-sitelock-to-be-acquired.html}}</ref> Previously based in [[Roseland, New Jersey]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://njbiz.com/comodo-ca-global-hq-coming-to-roseland/|title=Comodo CA global HQ coming to Roseland|last=Perry|first=Jessica|date=2018-07-03|website=NJBIZ|language=en-US|access-date=2019-10-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=May 1, 2018 |title=CBRE: Cybersecurity firm inks 20,000 sq. ft. in Roseland |url=https://re-nj.com/cbre-cybersecurity-firm-inks-20000-sq-ft-in-roseland/ |access-date=2026-07-30 |website=Real Estate NJ}}</ref> Sectigo has been headquartered in Scottsdale since 2023.<ref name=Gifford/> Approximately 26 employees, including 13 [[programmer]]s and [[software engineer]]s, work in the Phoenix metropolitan area as of 2025.<ref name=Gifford/>

Sectigo acquired [[Entrust]]'s public certificate business in early 2025. Prior to the purchase, Entrust allowed its customers to use certificates from Sectigo.<ref name="Rundle">{{cite news |last1=Rundle |first1=James |title=Sectigo Buys Entrust's Public Certificate Business |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/sectigo-buys-entrusts-public-certificate-business-6e476734 |work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=January 29, 2025}}</ref> The migration of Entrust's public certificate business included over half a million certificates and was completed in September 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lynn |first1=Samara |title=Sectigo Completes Entrust Certificate Migration Following Acquisition |url=https://www.mescomputing.com/news/security/sectigo-completes-entrust-certificate-migration-following-acquisition |date=September 29, 2025|work=MES Computing}}</ref> Sectigo also began offering Certificates as a Service (CaaS) in 2025.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Ian |title=CA/Browser Forum votes to reduce SSL/TLS certificates to 47 days |url=https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/2025/04/14/ca-browser-forum-votes-to-reduce-ssl-tls-certificates-to-42-days/ |work=Enterprise Times |date=April 14, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Murphy |first1=Ian |title=What will the change to 47-day SSL-TLS certificates mean to you? |url=https://www.enterprisetimes.co.uk/2025/04/18/what-will-the-change-to-47-day-ssl-tls-certificates-mean-to-you/ |work=Enterprise Times |date=April 18, 2025}}</ref> 
In 2026, Sectigo began offering Sectigo Partner Platform, a multi-tenant platform intended for use by [[managed service providers]] and channel partners to manage digital certificates and related lifecycle processes.<ref>{{cite web
 |title=Sectigo Targets MSP Growth with Multi-Tenant Certificate Management Platform
 |url=https://www.channelinsider.com/security/next-gen-solutions/sectigo-partner-platform-certificate-management/
 |website=Channel Insider
 |date=March 2026
 |access-date=April 24, 2026
}}</ref>

Sectigo is a [[Certificate Transparency]] log provider.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Korzhitskii |first=Nikita |last2=Carlsson |first2=Niklas |date=June 2020 |title=Characterizing the Root Landscape of Certificate Transparency Logs |url=https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/9142756 |journal=2020 IFIP Networking Conference (Networking) |pages=190–198}}</ref>
